From e2bb9fab08cbcc7922050c7eb0bd650807abfa4e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Kan Liang <kan.liang@linux.intel.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2021 08:32:38 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] perf/x86/intel/uncore: Fix invalid unit check

The uncore unit with the type ID 0 and the unit ID 0 is missed.

The table3 of the uncore unit maybe 0. The
uncore_discovery_invalid_unit() mistakenly treated it as an invalid
value.

Remove the !unit.table3 check.

Fixes: edae1f06c2cd ("perf/x86/intel/uncore: Parse uncore discovery tables")
Signed-off-by: Kan Liang <kan.liang@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Reviewed-by: Andi Kleen <ak@linux.intel.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/1629991963-102621-3-git-send-email-kan.liang@linux.intel.com

diff --git a/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h b/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h
index 7280c8a3c831..6d735611c281 100644
--- a/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h
+++ b/arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h
@@ -30,7 +30,7 @@
 
 
 #define uncore_discovery_invalid_unit(unit)			\
-	(!unit.table1 || !unit.ctl || !unit.table3 ||	\
+	(!unit.table1 || !unit.ctl || \
 	 unit.table1 == -1ULL || unit.ctl == -1ULL ||	\
 	 unit.table3 == -1ULL)
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/events/intel/uncore_discovery.h`**
   - The macro `uncore_discovery_invalid_unit(unit)` was modified by removing the check for `!unit.table3`. 
   - The updated macro now only checks for `!unit.table1`, `!unit.ctl`, and the conditions where `unit.table1`, `unit.ctl`, or `unit.table3` are equal to `-1ULL`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification addresses a bug where the uncore unit with type ID 0 and unit ID 0 was incorrectly treated as invalid due to the check on `unit.table3`. By removing this check, the patch ensures that valid uncore units are not mistakenly marked as invalid, thus improving the accuracy of the uncore discovery process. This change is directly related to the bug fix referenced in the patch, which aims to correct the handling of uncore unit discovery.

Here is the commit message:
perf/x86/intel/uncore: Fix invalid unit check

The uncore unit with the type ID 0 and the unit ID 0 is missed.

The table3 of the uncore unit maybe 0. The
uncore_discovery_invalid_unit() mistakenly treated it as an invalid
value.

Remove the !unit.table3 check.

Fixes: edae1f06c2cd ("perf/x86/intel/uncore: Parse uncore discovery tables")
Signed-off-by: Kan Liang <kan.liang@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Reviewed-by: Andi Kleen <ak@linux.intel.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/1629991963-102621-3-git-send-email-kan.liang@linux.intel.com

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the uncore unit with type ID 0 and unit ID 0, where the check for `!unit.table3` mistakenly classified it as an invalid unit, even though it could be a valid entry. This led to valid uncore units being incorrectly marked as invalid during the discovery process.

Here is the patch:
 
 #define uncore_discovery_invalid_unit(unit)			\
-	(!unit.table1 || !unit.ctl || !unit.table3 ||	\
+	(!unit.table1 || !unit.ctl || \
 	 unit.table1 == -1ULL || unit.ctl == -1ULL ||	\
 	 unit.table3 == -1ULL)

Reason:
The check for `!unit.table3` incorrectly classified a valid uncore unit (with type ID 0 and unit ID 0) as invalid, even though `table3` could legitimately be 0. This led to valid entries being marked as invalid during the discovery process.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
// Removed the check for !unit.table3
```
Reason:
By removing the `!unit.table3` check, the code now allows for valid uncore units with a `table3` value of 0 to be correctly recognized as valid, thus preventing the erroneous classification of valid units as invalid during the discovery process.
